macos-glass.builtBy: PROCTOR_SIGN_IDENTITY='Developer ID Application: Luke Rhodes (H4HGFL52W7)' bash scripts/build-app.sh
macos-glass.attachedBy: pid 88463 owns CG windows 43384 'History' and 43385 'Proctor' (640x572); glass_probe read it from CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo, the window server's own list. Launched with open -n because the installed build holds the same bundle id and LaunchServices activates it instead of starting a second instance — which is also why every capture names a CG window id rather than a title.
macos-glass.captureChannel: proctor_capture → ScreenCaptureKit window-scoped, frameStatus per frame; the menu bar extra through screencapture -R cropped to the AXExtrasMenuBar frame, because a status item is not a window Proctor owns

guest-glass.builtBy: PROCTOR_SIGN_IDENTITY='Developer ID Application: Luke Rhodes (H4HGFL52W7)' bash scripts/build-app.sh, then scripts/notarize.sh to submit and staple; copied into the guest and installed at /Applications/Proctor.app. The two binaries hash the same: sha256 8b0e0884d25a99d7d44f8d19f64b371257bcebc5cb00ea1056fe1f74bd59d37c on both sides, so the guest is running this build and not the 0.2.0 release.
guest-glass.attachedBy: Guest proctor-guest (lume, macOS 26.6.2 Tahoe), provisioned with lume create --unattended so it holds a real Aqua session: stat -f %Su /dev/console reads lume, not root, which is what the earlier proctor-mac-node clone could not offer. launchctl print gui/501/app.fledgeling.procter.agent reads state = running, pid = 1322. That agent's own proctor_doctor answers ready true with Accessibility and Screen Recording both granted, and lists attachedApps app:1085:1 Calculator windows 1 — the guest's accessibility API reading a window the guest's own window server owns. Reached from this Mac over an SSH StreamLocal forward between the two agents' unix sockets, with the host agent relaying.
guest-glass.captureChannel: lume VNC framebuffer read of the guest's virtual display via vncdotool. VNC carries no per-frame status, so frameStatus is recorded as unreported rather than claimed; the pixels are corroborated by the guest's own accessibility tree through proctor_find returning the same two strings the picture shows.
